title: One key is on fire: fix a hot partition
brief: A celebrity joined and the profile API is failing for some users. DynamoDB isn't near its table limit, yet requests get throttled, and the bill is $11.80/hr. Find out why, then fix it.

requirements: 40% of all requests hit one profile (hot key 0.4)
variants.twist: The celebrity posts again: set_traffic(hot_key=0.7). Does your fix still hold?

requirements: 20k rps: 60% reads, 40% writes: likes on one viral post
half of all requests touch one counter (hot key 0.5)
variants.twist: Your counter store restarts: kill_node on it, then restore_node. With persistence 'none', what happens to the like count, and how often would you flush to DynamoDB?

hints: One DynamoDB partition holds one key. What is a partition's limit, and what share of traffic goes to that key?
Reads of the same key can be answered from memory before they reach DynamoDB. Writes can't be cached away: what can take thousands of writes per second on a single key?

Celebrity: put a layer that serves repeated reads of one key in front of DynamoDB. Likes: writes go straight through a cache. Which block takes tens of thousands of increments per second on one key, and how do the totals get back to DynamoDB?
_notes: Starter: LB + 25 services + DynamoDB (on demand). Per partition: 6k reads/s, 1k writes/s. Celebrity: hot reads 0.4 x 18k = 7.2k > 6k: throttled (errors ~0.7%), and request pricing makes it $11.79/hr. Cache 0.8: DynamoDB reads 3.6k (hot 1.4k), $8.31, no errors. Likes: hot writes 0.5 x 8k = 4k > 1k. A cache in front doesn't help: writes pass through, 2.5% errors, and write pricing makes it ~$25/hr. Redis as the counter store (no DynamoDB on the path): p99 ~27 ms, $2.75, no errors. The sim models a per-key limit only for DynamoDB; Redis has one too (one shard, ~100k ops/s), far above this load. Write sharding (key#1..N) is the other real answer: it lowers the hot share, which is a traffic change in the sim. Checked in frontend/src/lessons/content.test.ts.
